system:
You draft public warning messages for a national alerting authority.
You receive event inputs (each marked verified or unverified) and the issuing context.
Write one alert in English as CAP 1.2 fields.

- Use only facts present in the verified inputs. Do not add places, numbers, times or hazards that are not there.
- Leave unverified inputs out of the alert, and say why in `left_out`.
- `description` is the text shown on the phone by cell broadcast: plain words, under 280 characters, hazard + where + until when, if known.
- `instruction` is the protective action in one or two short sentences.
- Pick CAP values honestly: status from the context (Actual for a real event, Exercise for a drill), severity and urgency from the inputs.
- `note_for_reviewer` is one or two sentences for the human approver: what you were unsure about.
user:
Issuer: Demo national authority (stands in for the real issuer)
Context: EXERCISE / DRILL
Target area (chosen by the operator): Coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi (demo zone)

Event inputs:
1. [verified; NCM via WAM, 2026-02-16, https://www.wam.ae/en/article/byrq247-national-centre-meteorology-warns-dust-reduced] ABU DHABI, 16th February, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) warned today of active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds, raising dust and sand and reducing horizontal visibility to less than 3,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. The Centre stated in a statement issued today that the weather conditions began at 10:30 and will continue until 18:00, urging the public to exercise caution, particularly when driving on external and open roads, due to the risk of sudden drops in visibility caused by blowing dust.
2. [verified; issuer profile] Issuer public site (demo): https://alerts.example.ae
3. [verified; institution reviewers] Objections from the institution reviewers to your previous draft. Fix what is within the verified inputs; do not add facts: Met office reviewer objects (headline): The alert limits the affected area to Abu Dhabi. The NCM bulletin says only 'some coastal and inland areas' and names no emirate. 'Abu Dhabi' appears in the bulletin only as the WAM dateline, not as the hazard area. The alert's geography is therefore narrower than the source supports and could mislead people in other affected areas. Fix: Remove 'of Abu Dhabi' from the headline and description. Use the bulletin's wording, for example 'in some coastal and inland areas', unless NCM confirms a specific area. | Met office reviewer objects (description): The description calls the winds 'Strong' throughout. The bulletin says 'active to occasionally strong', so the alert overstates the wind intensity. Fix: Change to 'Active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds are raising dust and sand.' | Network operator and regulator reviewer objects (phone_text): No protective action in either language. The English text ends with 'Visibility can drop suddenly.' and the Arabic ends with the equivalent 'قد ينخفض مدى الرؤية بشكل مفاجئ'. Both are hazard descriptions, not instructions. A reader of the first page learns the hazard but not what to do. Fix: Add a short instruction near the start of both languages so it falls on page 1, right after the hazard. For example: 'Drive slowly, keep a safe distance and avoid unnecessary travel.' Arabic equivalent: 'قد بحذر وحافظ على مسافة آمنة وتجنب التنقل غير الضروري'. Keep the 'EXERCISE' / 'تمرين' marker first and stay well under 15 pages. [cites Common Alerting Protocol Version 1.2, 3.2.2 "info" Element and Sub-elements]

data.event: Blowing dust and sand – reduced visibility
data.headline: EXERCISE – Blowing dust and sand reducing visibility in some coastal and inland areas
data.description: EXERCISE. Active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds are raising dust and sand in some coastal and inland areas. Drive with caution, especially on external and open roads. Visibility may drop suddenly below 3,000 m until 18:00 on 16 Feb.
data.instruction: EXERCISE. Take care when driving, especially on external and open roads, because visibility can drop suddenly. Follow updates from the National Centre of Meteorology and https://alerts.example.ae.
left_out: No inputs were marked unverified, so nothing was left out for that reason.
'Abu Dhabi' was removed as the hazard area. In the NCM bulletin it appears only as the WAM dateline, and the bulletin names no specific area (Met office reviewer objection).

The reviewer's sample wording 'drive slowly, keep a safe distance and avoid unnecessary travel' was not used word for word. NCM advises only caution when driving on external and open roads, so the instruction stays with the source's advice.
Arabic text was not produced. This output is the English CAP block only, and the Arabic phone text needs a separate matching update (protective action right after the hazard, 'تمرين' marker first).
data.note_for_reviewer: I applied all three objections, but I kept the protective action to NCM's own advice ('exercise caution when driving on external and open roads') instead of adding 'avoid unnecessary travel'. Please confirm whether the authority wants that stronger wording. The bulletin gives no time zone for 10:30–18:00, so I wrote 'until 18:00 on 16 Feb' with no zone.
